g.text: Mitochondrial DNA breaks trigger an all-or-none
Leave-one-mouse-out classifiers on Xenium 5k spatial transcriptomics

text.tspan: Mitochondrial dysfunction in oligodendrocytes (OLs) is
implicated in white-matter disease. In PlpTA:mtPst1 mice,
removing doxycycline induces double-strand breaks in OL
mitochondrial DNA (mtDSB).
This line shows demyelination of corpus callosum and
cerebellum 4-6 months after induction. What happens in the
tissue before that, and in which cells and regions?
Can the tissue itself tell which group a mouse belongs to,
and which genes does it use?
980 474 cells · 5 101 genes · 14 cell classes · 11 brain regions
Group comparisons (DESeq2, hierarchical Bayes) gave weak,
age-dependent effects. Averaging 3 responders with 3
non-responders explains both:
Bayesian case-control model: all 22 driver genes it tested
agree in direction (p < 1e-6), but shifts were small
'P21 modest / P60 strong' = 1 of 3 vs 2 of 3 responders; the
P21 responder is as strong as any.
Top 'mtDSB genes' Sgk1, Fkbp5 (stress hormones) varied between
sections, not with treatment.

g.text: 4 · Methods: let the tissue predict the mouse

text.tspan: Xenium 5k, 12 mice. Counts summed per
cell type x region x mouse
(pseudobulk) or kept per cell.
Disease-defined cluster (DA-OL) folded
into oligodendrocytes, so the model,
not the clustering, must find the
effect.
Train on 11 mice, predict the 12th;
repeat for every mouse. Ridge logistic
regression; permutation tests at the
mouse level.
Prespecified ISR gene score;
classifier score per OL; DA-OL cluster
share. Agreement between independent
inputs.
Correlate each gene with the OL score
within each section (removes batch,
plane, sacrifice time). Replicate
across cohorts.
The mouse is the unit: no cell is ever scored by a model that saw its mouse.
Confounds cannot create driver genes: they must vary between cells of the same section.
Independent of clustering: prior gene set, label-free classifier and cluster agree.
Replication: models trained on disjoint mice (P21-only vs P60-only) share top genes.

g.text: 5 · Only 3 of 6 mtDSB mice respond, and they respond strongly

text.tspan: Same 3 mice by three independent readouts.
ISR genes (Atf5, Trib3, Ddit3, Sesn2): no overlap with
controls; non-responders = controls.
mtDSB group 10x more variable than controls (p = 1e-4)
while means do not differ.
Not explained by sex, genotype, sample swap or
white-matter content.
Each mouse scored by models that never saw it. Filled orange = responders, open = non-responders, blue = controls.
34 up: ATF4 stress response, mitochondrial & protein quality control
(Hspa9, p62), p21, MHC-I and Cd40.
9 myelin genes down (Mog, Cnp, Cldn11, Mal).
Top genes replicate across cohorts (10/50 shared, p = 2e-11).

g.text: 7 · Where: brain-wide, strongest in thalamus and fiber tracts

text.tspan: Score = each OL's held-out p(mtDSB) as a percentile of control
OLs: responder OLs pile up at the top (median 65-85 vs 23-35 in
non-responders).
High-scoring OLs concentrate in the thalamus and the fiber-tract
arcs.
Thalamus and fiber tracts rank top on all three readouts; myelin
genes drop most there.
Controls vary (median 38-63); microglia in the responders turn
DAM-like (Cd74, Cst7 10-30x).
mtDSB causes an all-or-none OL stress response at 42 days: ISR + mitochondrial quality control, immune
visibility, myelin loss.
Responding OLs sit with DAM-like microglia in thalamus and white matter: a candidate prelude to
demyelination.
Why do 3 mice not respond? Testing induction (mtPstI qPCR, mtDNA damage) on remaining tissue.
Code, figures, tables: github.com/christoffermattssonlangseth/oligo-mtDSB
